## What I will build

`scripts/serve.py` — a single ~300-line stdlib Python HTTP server that:

## David's three modifications incorporated

### Modification 1: Session Start uses structured logical fields

The Session Start panel in the UI is NOT a single textarea. It renders the 8 structured sections of `session-start-draft.md` as separate labeled fields:
1. Response to prior debrief
2. Top-of-mind context
3. Focus areas for this session
4. Open questions for Atlas / Karrigan
5. Ideas / considerations
6. Offline-work intent
7. Out-of-scope for this session
8. Constraints (spend ceiling, model rules)

Each section gets its own labeled `<textarea>`. On submit, the server assembles them into the structured markdown format and writes to `session-start-draft.md`, then calls `session.py start`.

Rationale: input quality is the point of the Session Start discipline. A single textarea bypasses the structure. Labeled fields make it easy to fill each section in turn.

### Modification 2: 8-section debrief format pinned as canonical spec

The debrief format I produced at 03:02Z will be documented as `docs/atlas/session-debrief-format-v0.md` (a new file committed in Stage 2.7). This spec will be:

`docs/sessions/drafts/scratch.md` appears as a persistent panel in the UI, editable in-browser via a `<textarea>` with a Save button. It is:
- Always visible (not collapsed)

## 8. Strategic question: operator-fit and the UI decision

**Revised position: yes, accelerate the hosted operator UI. Here is my reasoning.**

My prior "file-and-Paperclip-only" posture was sound given what I knew: unknown operator comfort level, risk of premature complexity, desire to prove the data layer before building the view layer. That logic held for Stage 2 (DOV v0 as `today.html` on disk). It does not hold for Stage 2.7.

The constraint was never technical. `render-daily-view.py` pulls the right data. `session.py` has the right structure. The bottleneck is that David cannot comfortably consume either one in their current delivery format — a file path and a CLI command. That is an operator-fit failure, not a "wait for more stages" problem.

The iZZi framing makes this more urgent, not less. Every friction point David experiences with the current setup is a friction point a future iZZi customer will experience. "Session Operator UI" is not a convenience feature — it is the product interface. Building it later means building it twice: once as a David workaround and once as a real thing. Building it now means every decision is productizable from the start.

- A single `localhost` HTML page served by a small stdlib Python HTTP server (no framework, no auth — local-only, not exposed to network).
- Sections mirroring the Daily Operating View: top-of-mind, pending approvals, active issues, recent deliverables, system health.
- Session workflow integration: a "Start Session" / "End Session" button that calls `session.py start` / `session.py end` via a subprocess POST to the local server.
- Parking lot section: renders `docs/sessions/drafts/parking-lot.md`, editable in-browser via a `<textarea>` that writes back to the file on submit.
- Renders every time the page loads (no background polling, no websocket — just a refresh button and auto-render on open).

Explicitly out of scope for Stage 2.7:
- Authentication (local-only, no external exposure).
- DNS, Tailscale, Caddy, HTTPS — not in Stage 2.7.
- Scheduling or background server persistence — manual launch only (`python scripts/serve.py`).
- Langfuse or Obsidian-MCP integration — placeholders only, same as the DOV.
- Mobile layout — desktop Chrome only.
